6cab38fa1d9b.en: Actually working it out: two horses, the same stride after three steps

d215d988c366.zh: 取 $\eta=0.2$、$\varepsilon=0$（數字乾淨；實務會留一點 $\varepsilon$）。活躍維度 A 的歷史梯度是 $3,4,12$；安靜維度 B 是剛好小十倍的 $0.3,0.4,1.2$。看「有效學習率」$\eta/\sqrt{\sum g^{2}}$，以及用最後一筆梯度算出的實際步幅。
d215d988c366.en: Take $\eta=0.2$, $\varepsilon=0$ (clean numbers; in practice you keep a little $\varepsilon$). The past gradients of active dimension A are $3,4,12$; quiet dimension B has exactly ten times smaller ones, $0.3,0.4,1.2$. Look at the "effective learning rate" $\eta/\sqrt{\sum g^{2}}$, and the actual stride computed with the last gradient.

7cc258752ba8.zh: 步幅（有效學習率 $\times$ 最後一筆 $g$）

05d218c247de.zh: A 的當前梯度是 B 的十倍，但有效學習率被勒成 B 的十分之一，兩匹馬最後跨出的步幅都是 $0.185$。這就是「活躍維度被罰小步」的數字版：罰的不是「不准動」，是把韁繩勒緊，讓大梯度不要把參數甩飛。
05d218c247de.en: A's current gradient is ten times B's, but its effective learning rate is reined in to one tenth of B's, so both horses end up taking a stride of $0.185$. This is the numerical version of "active dimensions are penalized with small steps": the penalty is not "you may not move"; it is pulling the reins tight so a large gradient doesn't fling the parameter away.

33442a29dd92.zh: 再看長期隱憂。若某一維每步梯度都是 $1$、$\eta=1$、$\varepsilon=0$，有效學習率是 $1/\sqrt{k}$：
33442a29dd92.en: Now the long-term concern. If some dimension has gradient $1$ at every step, with $\eta=1$, $\varepsilon=0$, the effective learning rate is $1/\sqrt{k}$:

1a25597278b7.zh: 帳只會越記越厚，韁繩只會越勒越緊，最後所有維度的有效學習率都趨近 0——過早停止學習。這正是 KP-11 的 RMSProp 要拆掉的那根刺。
1a25597278b7.en: The ledger only gets thicker and the reins only get tighter, until in the end the effective learning rate of every dimension approaches 0 — learning stops prematurely. This is exactly the thorn that RMSProp in KP-11 sets out to remove.

928655a68a2f.zh: 直覺會說：「梯度大的維度比較重要，應該給它更大的學習率，讓它學快一點。」AdaGrad 做的剛好相反：梯度長期偏大的維度，有效學習率被壓小。原因不是討厭重要維度，而是那些維度已經走很遠了，再給大步會震盪；真正缺更新的，是那些幾乎沒被梯度光顧過的安靜維度。勒的是韁繩，不是把馬打死。
928655a68a2f.en: Intuition says: "Dimensions with large gradients are more important, so they should get a larger learning rate to learn faster." AdaGrad does exactly the opposite: dimensions whose gradients stay large get their effective learning rate pushed down. The reason is not that it dislikes important dimensions, but that those dimensions have already traveled far, and giving them big steps would make them oscillate; the ones that really lack updates are the quiet dimensions the gradient has barely visited. It is the reins being pulled, not the horse being killed.

388269414dd7.zh: 把「維度」換成「課堂發言」。話多的學生（活躍維度）被老師限時發言（有效學習率變小），話少的被點名多講一點。各維更新步幅才會趨於平衡。
388269414dd7.en: Swap "dimensions" for "speaking up in class". Talkative students (active dimensions) get a time limit from the teacher (smaller effective learning rate), and quiet ones get called on to say a bit more. That is how the update strides of all dimensions tend toward balance.

334019b093a8.zh: 自己算一題：$\eta=0.5$、$\varepsilon=0$，某維歷史梯度為 $6,8$。有效學習率是多少？若當前梯度仍是 $8$，步幅是多少？（提示：$\sum g^{2}=36+64=100$。）
334019b093a8.en: Work one out yourself: $\eta=0.5$, $\varepsilon=0$, and a dimension's past gradients are $6,8$. What is the effective learning rate? If the current gradient is still $8$, what is the stride? (Hint: $\sum g^{2}=36+64=100$.)

5e0aafdd728b.zh: 第一，「$\boldsymbol{G}$ 是 Hessian」。錯。$\boldsymbol{G}$ 只是梯度平方累加再開根號的對角矩陣，沒有二階導數。第二，「$\varepsilon$ 是動量或學習率」。錯。$\varepsilon$ 只是墊在分母裡防止除以零。第三，「AdaGrad 可以無限訓下去」。錯。累積和只增不減，長期有效學習率趨近 0，可能過早停學。
5e0aafdd728b.en: First, "$\boldsymbol{G}$ is the Hessian". Wrong. $\boldsymbol{G}$ is just a diagonal matrix of the square roots of accumulated squared gradients; there are no second derivatives. Second, "$\varepsilon$ is momentum or the learning rate". Wrong. $\varepsilon$ is only a shim in the denominator to prevent division by zero. Third, "AdaGrad can train forever". Wrong. The accumulated sum only grows, so in the long run the effective learning rate approaches 0 and learning may stop prematurely.

ecd60b457d21.zh: KP-2、KP-9 都還在用「一個全局 $\eta$」；AdaGrad 把 $\eta$ 拆成「每維一個有效值」。KP-5 的動量是平滑方向；AdaGrad 是縮放步幅——兩件不同的事。KP-11 會把「永不遺忘的累加」改成會遺忘的指數平均，並加上動量，變成 Adam。
ecd60b457d21.en: KP-2 and KP-9 still use "one global $\eta$"; AdaGrad splits $\eta$ into "one effective value per dimension". The momentum of KP-5 smooths the direction; AdaGrad scales the stride — two different things. KP-11 will turn the "never-forgetting accumulation" into an exponential average that forgets, and add momentum, giving Adam.

741a76cb3222.zh: AdaGrad 為每個維度累積梯度平方當分母：活躍維度被勒韁、罰小步，安靜維度獲較大有效學習率。優點是稀疏特徵走得動；隱憂是帳只增不減，最後大家都走不動。
741a76cb3222.en: AdaGrad accumulates squared gradients per dimension as the denominator: active dimensions are reined in and penalized with small steps, while quiet dimensions get a larger effective learning rate. The strength is that sparse features can still move; the concern is that the ledger only grows, so in the end nobody can move.

b93c21b5e15d.zh: 一句話收尾： 誰跑得兇誰被勒韁——活躍維度罰小步，齊步了，卻也可能把韁勒死。
b93c21b5e15d.en: One-line wrap-up: whoever runs hardest gets reined in — active dimensions are penalized with small steps; they fall into step, but the reins may end up choked tight.

740bc58b326a.zh: 教授祕笈：RMSProp 與 Adam——健忘油表加上剛發動校正
740bc58b326a.en: Professor's Secret Notes: RMSProp and Adam — a forgetful fuel gauge plus a just-started correction

354ec3aa8186.zh: 同學，KP-10 的 AdaGrad 把每滴油耗都記在帳上、永不擦掉，最後油門被勒死。這一站換一個主線比喻：健忘油表。RMSProp 不記一輩子的平方和，只記「最近的油耗」——舊帳會被遺忘。Adam 再把 KP-5 的動量方向接上去，但儀表剛發動時指針從 0 起跳、讀數偏低，所以要做偏置修正：用 $1/(1-\gamma^{k})$ 把指針拉回真實。今天會親手算一組 $\gamma=0.9$、$k=1$ 的修正因子——答案是整整 10 倍。
354ec3aa8186.en: Folks, AdaGrad in KP-10 wrote every drop of fuel consumption into the ledger and never erased it, until the throttle was finally strangled. At this stop we switch to a new main analogy: the forgetful fuel gauge. RMSProp doesn't keep a lifetime sum of squares; it only remembers "recent fuel consumption", and old entries get forgotten. Adam then hooks up the momentum direction from KP-5, but right after the gauge starts up, the needle jumps up from 0 and reads low, so we need bias correction: use $1/(1-\gamma^{k})$ to pull the needle back to the true value. Today you'll compute by hand the correction factor for $\gamma=0.9$, $k=1$, and the answer is a full 10 times.

1fa6eb97f3a4.zh: 一句話：RMSProp 用會遺忘的平方平均取代 AdaGrad 的死帳；Adam 再加動量，並把「剛發動讀數偏低」除以 $1-\gamma^{k}$ 校正回來。
1fa6eb97f3a4.en: In one sentence: RMSProp replaces AdaGrad's dead ledger with a squared average that can forget; Adam adds momentum on top and corrects the "too low right after starting up" readings by dividing by $1-\gamma^{k}$.

0c146a5cf5b0.zh: AdaGrad 的分母只增不減，訓久了有效學習率趨近 0。RMSProp 的靈感來自動量：不要累加，改成指數移動平均——每一步，舊記憶乘上遺忘因子 $\gamma$（常見 $0.9$），再摻一點新的梯度平方。舊的大梯度會慢慢淡出，學習率才不會被早期的一次暴衝永久鎖死。
0c146a5cf5b0.en: AdaGrad's denominator only ever grows, so after long training the effective learning rate approaches 0. RMSProp is inspired by momentum: don't accumulate, use an exponential moving average instead. At every step, the old memory is multiplied by the forgetting factor $\gamma$ (commonly $0.9$), and then a bit of the new squared gradient is mixed in. Old large gradients slowly fade out, so the learning rate isn't permanently locked down by a single early spike.

acc88b42c072.zh: Adam（Adaptive Moment Estimation）把兩件事焊在一起：一階矩 $\boldsymbol{m}$ 管方向（動量），二階矩 $v$ 管步幅（RMSProp 風格的平方平均）。大多數深度學習框架把它跟 mini-batch SGD 並列成預設選項。
acc88b42c072.en: Adam (Adaptive Moment Estimation) welds two things together: the first moment $\boldsymbol{m}$ handles direction (momentum), and the second moment $v$ handles step size (an RMSProp-style squared average). Most deep learning frameworks list it alongside mini-batch SGD as a default option.

e9a4c98936ea.zh: 還有一件容易被略過的事：$\boldsymbol{m}$ 和 $v$ 都從 0 開始。早期它們會系統性地偏小。不修正的話，前幾步等於故意踩小油門。偏置修正就是把被壓低的估計除以 $1-\gamma^{k}$ 拉回來；$k$ 變大後這個因子趨近 1，影響自動消失。
e9a4c98936ea.en: There's one more thing that's easy to skip over: $\boldsymbol{m}$ and $v$ both start at 0. Early on they are systematically too small. Without correction, the first few steps amount to deliberately going easy on the gas. Bias correction divides the suppressed estimates by $1-\gamma^{k}$ to pull them back up; as $k$ grows, this factor approaches 1 and the effect disappears on its own.

0c337468f7e7.en: Taking the symbols apart one by one (Eqs. (40)–(46))

07f85694e34b.zh: RMSProp 維護梯度平方的移動平均（式 (40)）：
07f85694e34b.en: RMSProp maintains a moving average of the squared gradient (Eq. (40)):

b63566552f01.en: $\gamma\in[0,1]$ is the forgetting factor. The update (Eq. (41)):

2284cb745cf4.zh: Adam 同時維護一階矩與二階矩（式 (42)、(43)）：
2284cb745cf4.en: Adam maintains the first and second moments at the same time (Eqs. (42), (43)):

dbcab66647ab.zh: 最終更新（式 (46)）是「帶動量的方向，除以自適應的步幅」：
dbcab66647ab.en: The final update (Eq. (46)) is "the momentum direction, divided by an adaptive step size":

c58c3116c396.zh: 真的算一遍：$\gamma=0.9$、$k=1$ 的修正因子
c58c3116c396.en: Let's actually compute it: the correction factor for $\gamma=0.9$, $k=1$

4ce5e64ff8d6.zh: 先算修正因子表。$\gamma=0.9$ 時，$\gamma^{1}=0.9$，所以
4ce5e64ff8d6.en: First, the table of correction factors. With $\gamma=0.9$, $\gamma^{1}=0.9$, so

7348b28562da.zh: 剛發動那一步，要把被壓低的矩估計放大十倍。後面幾步因子迅速掉回 1 附近：
7348b28562da.en: On the very first step after starting up, the suppressed moment estimate has to be scaled up tenfold. Over the next few steps the factor quickly drops back to around 1:

bc1a7796a2f8.zh: 配一組真實梯度看「拉回來」在幹嘛。令 $\gamma_{1}=\gamma_{2}=0.9$，$\boldsymbol{m}^{(0)}=0$、$v^{(0)}=0$，當前梯度 $g=4$，所以 $g^{2}=16$。
bc1a7796a2f8.en: Let's plug in a real gradient to see what "pulling back" is doing. Let $\gamma_{1}=\gamma_{2}=0.9$, $\boldsymbol{m}^{(0)}=0$, $v^{(0)}=0$, and current gradient $g=4$, so $g^{2}=16$.

0543288664e6.zh: 不修正時，第一步的方向長度只有約 $0.316$，整整被壓了三倍；修正後恰好是「單位化後的梯度方向」。這就是剛發動要校正指針的理由。
0543288664e6.en: Without correction, the length of the first step's direction is only about $0.316$, squashed by a full factor of three; after correction it is exactly "the normalized gradient direction". That's why the needle has to be corrected right after starting up.

57762e0c34e6.zh: 遺忘平方也可以對一下數字。設某維先來一筆 $g=10$（$g^{2}=100$），之後梯度為 0。AdaGrad 的分母至少永遠是 $\sqrt{100}=10$。RMSProp 從 $v=10$ 開始（第一步 $0.1\times 100$），之後每步乘 $0.9$：十步後 $10\times 0.9^{10}\approx 3.49$，二十步後 $\approx 1.22$。舊的暴衝被忘掉，油門重新活過來。
57762e0c34e6.en: We can also check the numbers for the forgetting squares. Suppose one dimension first gets a $g=10$ ($g^{2}=100$), and after that the gradient is 0. AdaGrad's denominator stays at least $\sqrt{100}=10$ forever. RMSProp starts at $v=10$ (first step: $0.1\times 100$), then gets multiplied by $0.9$ every step: after ten steps $10\times 0.9^{10}\approx 3.49$, after twenty steps $\approx 1.22$. The old spike is forgotten, and the throttle comes back to life.

066b072714ac.zh: 看到 $m$ 的公式裡有 $(1-\gamma_{1})g$，有人會覺得「第一步本來就該小，溫和起步比較穩」。Adam 的設計剛好相反：它認為那一下偏小不是溫和，是偏差——因為起始值是 0，不是因為你想保守。所以 $k=1$ 時硬把估計乘回 10，讓第一步看得到真正的梯度。溫和與否，該由 $\eta$ 決定，不該由「從零啟動」偷偷決定。
066b072714ac.en: Seeing $(1-\gamma_{1})g$ in the formula for $m$, some people think "the first step should be small anyway; a gentle start is more stable." Adam's design says exactly the opposite: it considers that small first step not gentleness but bias, because it's small only since the starting value is 0, not because you wanted to be conservative. So at $k=1$ it forcibly multiplies the estimate back by 10, letting the first step see the true gradient. Whether to be gentle should be decided by $\eta$, not secretly decided by "starting from zero".

f8a26dc363fb.zh: 把「矩估計」換成「體重計剛換電池」。指針從 0 爬升，前幾次讀數一定偏低；校正因子就是告訴你「現在只顯示了真實值的 $1-\gamma^{k}$，請除回去」。
f8a26dc363fb.en: Replace "moment estimate" with "a bathroom scale that just got new batteries". The needle climbs up from 0, so the first few readings are bound to be low; the correction factor tells you "right now it only shows $1-\gamma^{k}$ of the true value, so divide it back".

141bdb02ef44.zh: 自己算一題：$\gamma=0.9$、$k=2$，修正因子是多少？若未修正的 $m=0.58$，修正後的 $\widehat{m}$ 是多少？（提示：$0.9^{2}=0.81$。）
141bdb02ef44.en: Try one yourself: with $\gamma=0.9$, $k=2$, what is the correction factor? If the uncorrected $m=0.58$, what is the corrected $\widehat{m}$? (Hint: $0.9^{2}=0.81$.)

a3626624fb78.zh: 第一，「Adam 的一階矩、二階矩是權重的均值與方差」。錯。它們是梯度的動量與平方移動平均，不是參數本身的統計量。第二，「偏置修正是為了找尖銳極小值或取代正規化」。錯。它只補償 $m$、$v$ 從 0 啟動造成的系統性偏低。第三，「RMSProp 跟 AdaGrad 分母一樣都在無限累加」。錯。RMSProp 會遺忘，這正是它相對 AdaGrad 的關鍵改進。
a3626624fb78.en: First, "Adam's first and second moments are the mean and variance of the weights". Wrong. They are the momentum and squared moving average of the gradient, not statistics of the parameters themselves. Second, "bias correction is for finding sharp minima or replacing regularization". Wrong. It only compensates for the systematic underestimate caused by $m$ and $v$ starting from 0. Third, "RMSProp's denominator accumulates without bound, just like AdaGrad's". Wrong. RMSProp forgets, and that is exactly its key improvement over AdaGrad.

6af1521d9a8c.zh: KP-5 的動量就是 Adam 的 $\boldsymbol{m}$；KP-10 的 AdaGrad 就是「不會遺忘的 $v$」。KP-7、KP-8 的 SGD／mini-batch 仍是骨架，Adam 是在這副骨架上加方向平滑與逐維步幅。KP-9 提醒固定步長會在帶子裡晃——Adam 沒有取消 $\eta$，它只是讓各維的有效步長不再共用同一個數字。
6af1521d9a8c.en: The momentum from KP-5 is exactly Adam's $\boldsymbol{m}$; the AdaGrad from KP-10 is exactly "a $v$ that never forgets". The SGD / mini-batch from KP-7 and KP-8 is still the skeleton; Adam adds direction smoothing and per-dimension step sizes on top of that skeleton. KP-9 reminded us that a fixed step size makes you wobble inside a band; Adam doesn't remove $\eta$, it just stops making every dimension share the same effective step size.

7ddb74a1509e.zh: RMSProp 用指數平均遺忘舊的梯度平方，避免學習率被勒死；Adam 再加動量，並用 $1/(1-\gamma^{k})$ 把剛發動偏低的讀數拉回。$\gamma=0.9$、$k=1$ 時修正因子是 10。
7ddb74a1509e.en: RMSProp forgets old squared gradients with an exponential average, so the learning rate doesn't get strangled; Adam adds momentum on top and uses $1/(1-\gamma^{k})$ to pull back the low readings right after starting up. With $\gamma=0.9$, $k=1$, the correction factor is 10.

13c986325f41.zh: 一句話收尾： 舊帳要忘、剛發動要校正——$\gamma=0.9$ 的第一步，指針得乘回十倍才是真的。
13c986325f41.en: One-line wrap-up: Forget the old ledger, correct right after starting up: on the first step with $\gamma=0.9$, the needle has to be multiplied back by ten to read true.

cfbac49470e8.zh: 教授祕笈：平坦極小值與 SAM 動機——針尖站不住，寬碗才穩
cfbac49470e8.en: Professor's Secret Notes: flat minima and the motivation for SAM — you can't stand on a needle tip, but a wide bowl is stable

6add0a0d37d3.zh: 同學，反向傳播能找到「局部最低點」，但最低點長得不一樣。主線比喻就一個：針尖 vs 寬碗。針尖（sharp minimum）在最優點損失確實很低，可旁邊幾乎垂直——參數稍偏、測試資料稍變，損失就飆。寬碗（flat minimum）碗底損失未必是全場最低，但整圈都低，晃一晃還在碗裡。經驗上，寬碗往往比較能泛化；SAM 的動機，就是不要只挖針尖，要主動找寬碗。
6add0a0d37d3.en: Folks, backpropagation can find a "local lowest point", but not all lowest points look the same. There's just one main analogy: needle tip vs. wide bowl. At its optimum the needle tip (sharp minimum) really does have a very low loss, but the sides are almost vertical: shift the parameters a little, change the test data a little, and the loss shoots up. The bottom of the wide bowl (flat minimum) isn't necessarily the lowest loss anywhere, but the whole ring around it is low, so after a bit of shaking you're still in the bowl. Empirically, wide bowls tend to generalize better; the motivation for SAM is don't just dig needle tips, actively look for wide bowls.

5bbf9feeaed0.zh: 一句話：不是所有局部極小值都一樣好；鄰域裡損失幾乎不變的寬碗，通常比旁邊立刻變陡的針尖更禁得起擾動——SAM 就是為了把優化目標改成「整圈都低」。
5bbf9feeaed0.en: In one sentence: not all local minima are equally good; a wide bowl, where the loss barely changes across the neighborhood, usually withstands perturbations better than a needle tip that gets steep right next to it. SAM exists to change the optimization objective to "low all the way around".

221fb3bb4bd3.zh: 先講畫面，再講公式。Fig. 6 對比兩種谷：
221fb3bb4bd3.en: Picture first, formulas second. Fig. 6 compares two kinds of valley:

4a5e2ce53e2a.zh: 針尖（sharp）：解像站在針尖上，損失在最優點附近急劇上升。
4a5e2ce53e2a.en: Needle tip (sharp): the solution is like standing on the tip of a needle; the loss rises steeply around the optimum.

6f86627c9fa3.zh: 寬碗（flat）：解像坐在寬碗底，鄰域內損失幾乎保持不變。
6f86627c9fa3.en: Wide bowl (flat): the solution is like sitting at the bottom of a wide bowl; the loss stays almost unchanged across the neighborhood.

ee95771898d7.zh: 「平坦」指的不是「損失值比較高或比較低」，而是對參數微擾不敏感。測試時權重有量化誤差、資料有分佈偏移，都等價於你在解附近被推了一把——針尖上那一把是墜崖，寬碗裡那一把還在碗底。
ee95771898d7.en: "Flat" doesn't mean "the loss value is higher or lower"; it means insensitive to small perturbations of the parameters. Quantization error in the weights at test time, or a distribution shift in the data, are both equivalent to getting pushed near the solution: on a needle tip that push sends you off a cliff, in a wide bowl it leaves you at the bottom of the bowl.

449d1d91f8e3.zh: 這個主張有經驗支持，但文獻裡仍在辯論：平坦度不是泛化的唯一原因，隱式正則化、資料結構也可能幫忙。所以這一站的正確態度是「寬碗是值得追的方向」，不是「寬碗已被定理保證一定贏」。
449d1d91f8e3.en: This claim has empirical support, but it is still debated in the literature: flatness isn't the only cause of generalization; implicit regularization and the structure of the data may also help. So the right attitude at this stop is "a wide bowl is a direction worth chasing", not "a theorem guarantees the wide bowl always wins".

3e780a308ead.zh: 回顧 KP-1：一階方法（尤其 SGD）傾向掉進較平坦的谷，二階方法比較會鑽進針尖。這提供一條從「選算法」到「泛化」的直覺橋。SAM 則更進一步：不靠算法的偶然偏好，而是改寫目標，主動懲罰鄰域裡的高損失。
3e780a308ead.en: Recall KP-1: first-order methods (especially SGD) tend to fall into flatter valleys, while second-order methods are more likely to burrow into needle tips. This provides an intuitive bridge from "choosing an algorithm" to "generalization". SAM goes a step further: instead of relying on an algorithm's accidental preference, it rewrites the objective and actively penalizes high loss in the neighborhood.

d7909faea28c.zh: 符號逐個拆（動機層，公式細節留給 KP-13）
d7909faea28c.en: Taking the symbols apart one by one (motivation level; the formula details are left to KP-13)

e71b6c77e031.zh: 只在乎當前這一點低不高。SAM 的動機是改成「看整圈」：在半徑 $\rho$ 的鄰域裡，先找損失最大的那一推，再讓 $\boldsymbol{w}$ 去壓低那個最壞情況。白話就是——
e71b6c77e031.en: which only cares whether this one current point is low. The motivation for SAM is to switch to "looking all the way around": within a neighborhood of radius $\rho$, first find the push that gives the largest loss, then have $\boldsymbol{w}$ drive that worst case down. In plain words:

1de735a69733.zh: 針尖：單點很低，旁邊很高 $\rightarrow$ 最壞情況很慘，SAM 會重罰。
1de735a69733.en: Needle tip: very low at a single point, very high right beside it $\rightarrow$ the worst case is terrible, and SAM penalizes it heavily.

8892344137dc.zh: 寬碗：單點未必最低，但旁邊也不高 $\rightarrow$ 最壞情況仍然低，SAM 喜歡。
8892344137dc.en: Wide bowl: not necessarily the lowest at a single point, but not high beside it either $\rightarrow$ the worst case is still low, and SAM likes it.

6c2c20233a85.zh: min-max 的精確寫法與 $\boldsymbol{\epsilon}^{*}$ 的求法是 KP-13 的 Vanilla SAM；這裡只要抓住動機：懲罰銳度（sharpness），逼算法離開針尖、走進寬碗。
6c2c20233a85.en: The exact min-max formulation and how to find $\boldsymbol{\epsilon}^{*}$ are the Vanilla SAM of KP-13; here you only need to grasp the motivation: penalize sharpness, forcing the algorithm off the needle tip and into the wide bowl.

8db1416bedfc.zh: 真的算一遍：看起來更低的針尖，一晃就摔
8db1416bedfc.en: Let's actually compute it: the needle tip that looks lower falls over at the first wobble

a8f75bc79fd9.zh: 設一維玩具損失。針尖在 $w=0$ 確實比較低，寬碗比較「墊高」一點，但碗很開：
a8f75bc79fd9.en: Take a one-dimensional toy loss. At $w=0$ the needle tip really is lower, and the wide bowl sits a bit "raised", but the bowl is very open:

b026e910ef8d.zh: 只看最優點，$0.01\lt 0.08$，普通梯度下降會覺得針尖比較香。現在允許參數（或測試條件）偏離 $0.1$、$0.2$、$0.5$，並用 SAM 式的鄰域半徑 $\rho=0.2$ 看「最壞損失」。
b026e910ef8d.en: Looking only at the optimum, $0.01\lt 0.08$, so ordinary gradient descent would find the needle tip more appealing. Now let the parameters (or test conditions) deviate by $0.1$, $0.2$, $0.5$, and use a SAM-style neighborhood radius $\rho=0.2$ to look at the "worst-case loss".

33789bbe0195.zh: SAM 若看 $\rho=0.2$ 鄰域內的最大損失：針尖是 $2.01$，寬碗是 $0.10$——差二十倍。普通訓練會選針尖；看整圈的人會選寬碗。這就是「平坦可能更好」的數字版：泛化在意的是被推一把之後還剩多少，不是你在針尖上拍到的那張最低分。
33789bbe0195.en: If SAM looks at the maximum loss within the $\rho=0.2$ neighborhood: the needle tip gives $2.01$, the wide bowl gives $0.10$, a factor of twenty apart. Ordinary training would pick the needle tip; someone who looks all the way around would pick the wide bowl. This is the numerical version of "flat may be better": what generalization cares about is how much is left after you get pushed, not the single lowest score you snapped while standing on the needle tip.

30325647579a.zh: 訓練曲線上「訓練損失更低」的那個解，看起來像贏家。上面那張表把這份直覺翻過來：針尖在 $w=0$ 贏了 $0.07$，可是偏個 $0.2$ 就輸了將近 $2$。如果你以為「最低點一定最好」，你已經站上針尖了。SAM 要你改問：旁邊那圈高不高？
30325647579a.en: On the training curve, the solution with "the lower training loss" looks like the winner. The table above flips that intuition: the needle tip wins by $0.07$ at $w=0$, but shift it by $0.2$ and it loses by nearly $2$. If you think "the lowest point is always best", you're already standing on a needle tip. SAM wants you to ask instead: is the ring around it high or not?

529e26af63d0.zh: 把參數擾動換成「停車」。針尖是把車停在山脊的刀刃上，座標完美，一陣風就滑下山。寬碗是停在盆地，位置差幾公分無關痛癢。測試資料的偏移就是那陣風。
529e26af63d0.en: Replace parameter perturbation with "parking". The needle tip is parking your car on the knife edge of a mountain ridge: perfect coordinates, and one gust of wind sends it sliding down the mountain. The wide bowl is parking in a basin, where being a few centimeters off doesn't matter at all. A shift in the test data is that gust of wind.

15e1c851eade.zh: 自己算一題：若寬碗改成 $f(w)=0.08+2w^{2}$，在 $\lvert w\rvert=0.2$ 時損失是多少？還比針尖的 $2.01$ 低嗎？（提示：先算 $2\times 0.04$。）
15e1c851eade.en: Try one yourself: if the wide bowl becomes $f(w)=0.08+2w^{2}$, what is the loss at $\lvert w\rvert=0.2$? Is it still lower than the needle tip's $2.01$? (Hint: compute $2\times 0.04$ first.)

9f78934bb797.zh: 第一，「平坦極小值已被嚴格證明一定泛化更好」。錯。有經驗支持，文獻仍在辯論，平坦度不是唯一因素。第二，「平坦＝損失值比較高，所以比較差」。錯。平坦描述的是鄰域形狀，不是單點高低。第三，「SAM 是用來加速每步計算或取代反向傳播」。錯。它改的是優化目標（懲罰鄰域高損失），計算上往往更貴，細節見 KP-13。
9f78934bb797.en: First, "flat minima have been rigorously proven to always generalize better". Wrong. There is empirical support, the literature is still debating it, and flatness is not the only factor. Second, "flat = higher loss value, so it's worse". Wrong. Flatness describes the shape of the neighborhood, not how high a single point is. Third, "SAM is for speeding up each step's computation or replacing backpropagation". Wrong. What it changes is the optimization objective (penalizing high loss in the neighborhood), and it is often more expensive to compute; see KP-13 for details.

540afc00925e.zh: KP-1 已說過：一階方法傾向較平坦的谷，二階方法容易鑽針尖。KP-7 的 SGD 雜訊，常被認為有把解推向寬碗的副作用。KP-9 的「$\eta$ 寬帶子」是另一種「停在鄰域裡晃」——那是收斂精度的帶子；這裡的寬碗是損失地形的形狀，別把兩件事當成同一個 $\eta$。KP-13 會把動機寫成真正的 min-max 公式。
540afc00925e.en: KP-1 already said it: first-order methods tend toward flatter valleys, while second-order methods tend to burrow into needle tips. The SGD noise of KP-7 is often thought to have the side effect of pushing the solution toward wide bowls. The "$\eta$-wide band" of KP-9 is another kind of "wobbling around inside a neighborhood", but that is a band of convergence precision; the wide bowl here is the shape of the loss landscape, so don't treat the two as the same $\eta$ thing. KP-13 will write the motivation as an actual min-max formula.

9cecff88f489.zh: 局部極小值有針尖與寬碗兩種長相：針尖單點很低、旁邊驟升；寬碗整圈都低、較禁得起擾動。經驗上寬碗常較能泛化，但仍在辯論。SAM 的動機是懲罰鄰域最大損失，主動離開針尖。
9cecff88f489.en: Local minima come in two shapes, needle tips and wide bowls: a needle tip is very low at a single point and rises steeply beside it; a wide bowl is low all the way around and withstands perturbations better. Empirically wide bowls often generalize better, but this is still debated. The motivation for SAM is to penalize the maximum loss in the neighborhood and actively leave the needle tip.

f2a4c80d4f41.zh: 一句話收尾： 別站針尖——要坐寬碗；SAM 看的不是單點多低，是整圈晃不晃得住。
f2a4c80d4f41.en: One-line wrap-up: Don't stand on a needle tip, sit in a wide bowl; SAM doesn't look at how low a single point is, but at whether the whole ring holds up when shaken.

0adf0bb0ebfc.zh: 教授祕笈：Vanilla SAM——先走到最慘鄰居再下山
0adf0bb0ebfc.en: Professor's Secret Notes: Vanilla SAM, walk to the worst neighbor first, then go downhill

745410f82f9b.zh: 一句話地圖，一個比喻貫通
745410f82f9b.en: A One-Sentence Map, One Analogy That Ties It All Together

886eaf442911.zh: 主線比喻是「先走到最慘鄰居再下山」。平常的梯度下降像在霧裡找山谷：腳下哪裡陡，就往反方向走一步。Sharpness-Aware Minimization（SAM，銳度感知最小化）更龜毛——它不相信「我站的這一點損失低」就夠了，一定要先走到隔壁最慘的鄰居（半徑 $\rho$ 的球裡、損失最高的那一點），確認整圈鄰域都站得住，才從那裡量斜率下山。整節式 (47)–(53) 就是把這套「先探最慘鄰居」的流程寫成數學。
886eaf442911.en: The main analogy is "walk to the worst neighbor first, then go downhill". Ordinary gradient descent is like looking for a valley in the fog: wherever it's steep underfoot, you take a step the opposite way. Sharpness-Aware Minimization (SAM) is pickier: it doesn't trust that "the point I'm standing on has low loss" is enough. It insists on first walking over to the worst neighbor next door (the point with the highest loss inside the ball of radius $\rho$), making sure the whole surrounding neighborhood holds up, and only then measuring the slope from there to go downhill. All of Eqs. (47)–(53) in this section just write this "probe the worst neighbor first" procedure as math.

48d53515d6b0.zh: 先講一句白話、一個符號都不要：不是所有谷底都一樣好。 尖銳的谷（sharp）像一條窄溝，訓練點損失很低，風一吹（換測試資料、權重稍微晃一下）損失就暴衝；平坦的谷（flat）像寬淺盆地，你在附近走一圈損失幾乎不變，往往泛化比較好——這是 KP-12 的動機，SAM 是把它變成可優化的目標。
48d53515d6b0.en: First, one plain sentence, not a single symbol: not all valley floors are equally good. A sharp valley is like a narrow ditch: the loss at the training point is very low, but at the slightest breeze (switching to test data, the weights wobbling a little) the loss shoots up. A flat valley is like a wide, shallow basin: walk a lap around it and the loss barely changes, and it often generalizes better. That is KP-12's motivation; SAM turns it into an objective you can optimize.

83f92a6e8dab.zh: 為什麼需要它？反向傳播只會把訓練損失往下推，它不管谷是尖是平。SAM 的解法是：先在半徑 $\rho$ 的小球裡找最壞鄰居，再最小化那個最壞損失，逼你的解「整個鄰域」都得低。
83f92a6e8dab.en: Why do we need it? Backpropagation only pushes the training loss down; it doesn't care whether the valley is sharp or flat. SAM's fix: first find the worst neighbor inside a small ball of radius $\rho$, then minimize that worst loss, forcing your solution to be low over its "whole neighborhood".

21b5811cd043.zh: $\boldsymbol{w}$ 是網路權重，$\mathcal{L}(\cdot)$ 是訓練損失，$\rho\geq 0$ 是鄰域半徑（超參數），$p$ 是範數種類（建議 $p=2$），$\boldsymbol{\epsilon}$ 是加在權重上的小擾動。
21b5811cd043.en: $\boldsymbol{w}$ is the network weights, $\mathcal{L}(\cdot)$ is the training loss, $\rho\geq 0$ is the neighborhood radius (a hyperparameter), $p$ is the type of norm ($p=2$ recommended), and $\boldsymbol{\epsilon}$ is a small perturbation added to the weights.

c886f9f504b2.en: Drop $\lambda\|\boldsymbol{w}\|_2^2$ and you get the pure min-max (Eq. 49):

9d3be962e9ec.zh: 白話：內層 maximize＝走進最慘鄰居；外層 minimize＝讓那個最慘損失也變小。拆開來看（式 50）：
9d3be962e9ec.en: In plain words: the inner maximize = walk into the worst neighbor; the outer minimize = make that worst loss small too. Split apart (Eq. 50):

43537229f0be.zh: 銳度就是「鄰域內損失最多能漲多少」——越大，谷越尖。
43537229f0be.en: Sharpness is just "how much the loss can rise at most within the neighborhood": the larger it is, the sharper the valley.

140a81070175.zh: 內層不好解，用一階泰勒 $\mathcal{L}(\boldsymbol{w}+\boldsymbol{\epsilon})\approx\mathcal{L}(\boldsymbol{w})+\boldsymbol{\epsilon}^{\top}\nabla_{\boldsymbol{w}}\mathcal{L}(\boldsymbol{w})$，問題變成在 $\|\boldsymbol{\epsilon}\|_p\leq\rho$ 下最大化 $\boldsymbol{\epsilon}^{\top}\nabla\mathcal{L}$。一般解是對偶範數公式（式 51，$1/p+1/q=1$）；當 $p=2$ 時大幅簡化成式 (52)：
140a81070175.en: The inner problem is hard to solve, so use a first-order Taylor expansion $\mathcal{L}(\boldsymbol{w}+\boldsymbol{\epsilon})\approx\mathcal{L}(\boldsymbol{w})+\boldsymbol{\epsilon}^{\top}\nabla_{\boldsymbol{w}}\mathcal{L}(\boldsymbol{w})$; the problem becomes maximizing $\boldsymbol{\epsilon}^{\top}\nabla\mathcal{L}$ subject to $\|\boldsymbol{\epsilon}\|_p\leq\rho$. The general solution is the dual-norm formula (Eq. 51, $1/p+1/q=1$); when $p=2$ it simplifies greatly to Eq. (52):

cf6e5a2b1a73.zh: 就是：沿梯度方向（損失上升最快）、長度剛好為 $\rho$ 的那一步。 把 $\boldsymbol{\epsilon}^*$ 代回，對 $\boldsymbol{w}$ 求梯度，並忽略 $d\boldsymbol{\epsilon}^*/d\boldsymbol{w}$ 的次要項，得到式 (53)：
cf6e5a2b1a73.en: That is: the step along the gradient direction (where the loss rises fastest) with length exactly $\rho$. Substitute $\boldsymbol{\epsilon}^*$ back, take the gradient with respect to $\boldsymbol{w}$, ignore the second-order term in $d\boldsymbol{\epsilon}^*/d\boldsymbol{w}$, and you get Eq. (53):

5ed58c284ab0.zh: 實作三步：(1) 在 $\boldsymbol{w}$ 算梯度；(2) 用式 (52) 得到 $\boldsymbol{\epsilon}^*$，ascent 走到 $\boldsymbol{w}+\boldsymbol{\epsilon}^*$；(3) 在擾動點再算一次梯度，用它對原本的 $\boldsymbol{w}$ 做 descent。所以 Vanilla SAM 每步大約是普通 SGD 的兩倍反傳。
5ed58c284ab0.en: Implementation in three steps: (1) compute the gradient at $\boldsymbol{w}$; (2) get $\boldsymbol{\epsilon}^*$ from Eq. (52) and take an ascent step to $\boldsymbol{w}+\boldsymbol{\epsilon}^*$; (3) compute the gradient once more at the perturbed point and use it for a descent step on the original $\boldsymbol{w}$. So each step of Vanilla SAM costs about twice the backward passes of plain SGD.

c21feefa60e0.en: The gradient is $\nabla_{\boldsymbol{w}}\mathcal{L}(\boldsymbol{w})=(3,4)$, with Euclidean length

a356a9f78c6a.en: Check the length: $\|(0.06,0.08)\|_{2}=\sqrt{0.0036+0.0064}=\sqrt{0.01}=0.1=\rho$. The direction is exactly the gradient's unit vector, not reversed at all.

034fc8f16362.zh: 假設目前站在 $\boldsymbol{w}=(1.00,\;2.00)$，最慘鄰居就是
034fc8f16362.en: Suppose we are currently standing at $\boldsymbol{w}=(1.00,\;2.00)$; the worst neighbor is then

6866eb64b6d5.zh: 若原點損失 $\mathcal{L}(\boldsymbol{w})=0.50$、擾動點 $\mathcal{L}(\boldsymbol{w}+\boldsymbol{\epsilon}^{*})=0.73$，銳度項（式 50）就是 $0.73-0.50=0.23$。SAM 不會用 $(3,4)$ 這個原點梯度去下山，而是跑到 $(1.06,2.08)$ 再算一次梯度，用那裡的斜率更新 $\boldsymbol{w}$。
6866eb64b6d5.en: If the loss at the original point is $\mathcal{L}(\boldsymbol{w})=0.50$ and at the perturbed point $\mathcal{L}(\boldsymbol{w}+\boldsymbol{\epsilon}^{*})=0.73$, the sharpness term (Eq. 50) is $0.73-0.50=0.23$. SAM does not go downhill with the original-point gradient $(3,4)$; it goes to $(1.06,2.08)$, computes the gradient again, and updates $\boldsymbol{w}$ with the slope there.

fb6ad5b713b4.en: Go downhill with the slope here

82a179c8ee44.en: Loss difference between the two points

6985846293aa.zh: 直覺會說：「要找低損失，當然直接下山啊，幹嘛先往上走？」SAM 的反轉是：往上走不是為了待在高處，是為了摸清這座谷有多尖。 你先被推到最慘鄰居，再從那裡量斜率——如果連最慘鄰居的損失都能被壓下去，整圈鄰域就被迫變平。看起來多走冤枉路，其實是在買泛化保險。還有一個容易忽略的細節：式 (52) 文獻裡也討論過，它比較像誤差上界的方向，不是銳度的精確界；實務上我們仍用它，因為好算、也夠用。
6985846293aa.en: Intuition says: "If you want low loss, obviously you just go downhill. Why walk uphill first?" SAM's twist: going uphill isn't about staying up high; it's about finding out how sharp this valley is. You get pushed to the worst neighbor first, then measure the slope from there. If even the worst neighbor's loss can be pushed down, the whole surrounding neighborhood is forced to become flat. It looks like a pointless detour, but you're actually buying generalization insurance. One more easily overlooked detail: the literature has also discussed that Eq. (52) is more like the direction of an upper bound on the error, not an exact bound on the sharpness. In practice we still use it, because it's cheap to compute and good enough.

cce4204cc308.en: The Way Out: Generalize from Here

c55f995abff1.zh: 同一套「先找最壞再最小化」其實就是對抗訓練、強健最佳化的骨架：圖片加一點最能騙過模型的雜訊，再讓模型把這張「最慘圖」也分對。現在換數字自己算一次（答案不公佈）：$\rho=0.2$、$\nabla\mathcal{L}=(5,12)$，請寫出 $\boldsymbol{\epsilon}^{*}$ 與 $\|\boldsymbol{\epsilon}^{*}\|_{2}$。提示：先算 $\|\nabla\mathcal{L}\|_{2}$，再套式 (52)。若你算出長度不是 $0.2$，多半是忘了除以範數。
c55f995abff1.en: The same "find the worst case first, then minimize" recipe is in fact the skeleton of adversarial training and robust optimization: add a little noise to an image that best fools the model, then make the model classify that "worst image" correctly too. Now change the numbers and compute it yourself (answer not given): $\rho=0.2$, $\nabla\mathcal{L}=(5,12)$; write down $\boldsymbol{\epsilon}^{*}$ and $\|\boldsymbol{\epsilon}^{*}\|_{2}$. Hint: first compute $\|\nabla\mathcal{L}\|_{2}$, then apply Eq. (52). If the length you get isn't $0.2$, you most likely forgot to divide by the norm.

2d9ba842e5fd.zh: 誤解「SAM 就是再加一層 L2 正則」。式 (47) 的 $\lambda\|\boldsymbol{w}\|_2^2$ 是另外可加的權重衰減；銳度項是鄰域內的損失增量，不是權重大小。
2d9ba842e5fd.en: Misconception: "SAM is just one more layer of L2 regularization." The $\lambda\|\boldsymbol{w}\|_2^2$ in Eq. (47) is weight decay that can be added separately; the sharpness term is the loss increase within the neighborhood, not the size of the weights.

20325ccd3949.zh:
誤解「$ oldsymbol{\epsilon}^{*}=ho
abla\mathcal{L}$」。少了除以 $\|
abla\mathcal{L}\|_2$，擾動長度會變成 $ho\|
abla\mathcal{L}\|$ 而不是 $ho$。上面例子若忘了除 $5$，會得到 $(0.3,0.4)$，長度 $0.5$，整整大了五倍。
20325ccd3949.en:
Misconception: "$ oldsymbol{\epsilon}^{*}=ho
abla\mathcal{L}$." Without dividing by $\|
abla\mathcal{L}\|_2$, the perturbation length becomes $ho\|
abla\mathcal{L}\|$ instead of $ho$. In the example above, forgetting to divide by $5$ gives $(0.3,0.4)$, with length $0.5$, a full five times too big.

0648955e6442.zh: 誤解「梯度還是在原點算」。式 (53) 明講：下山用的斜率是在 $\boldsymbol{w}+\boldsymbol{\epsilon}^{*}$ 算的。若改成 $-\rho\nabla/\|\nabla\|$，那是往最好鄰居走，方向整個反掉。
0648955e6442.en: Misconception: "the gradient is still computed at the original point." Eq. (53) says it plainly: the slope used to go downhill is computed at $\boldsymbol{w}+\boldsymbol{\epsilon}^{*}$. If you change it to $-\rho\nabla/\|\nabla\|$, you are walking toward the best neighbor, and the direction is completely reversed.

084d07745b75.zh: KP-12：平坦 vs 尖銳極小值的動機與 Fig. 6；本節把「喜歡平坦」寫成 min-max。
084d07745b75.en: KP-12: the motivation of flat vs. sharp minima and Fig. 6; this section writes "prefer flat" as a min-max.

4b8eb6616d69.zh: KP-2：外層仍是梯度下降，只是梯度的計算點換到最慘鄰居。
4b8eb6616d69.en: KP-2: the outer level is still gradient descent; only the point where the gradient is computed moves to the worst neighbor.

cf854da5e1b0.zh: KP-6：每步兩次反向傳播，鏈式法則沒變，只是多跑一趟 ascent。
cf854da5e1b0.en: KP-6: two backpropagation passes per step; the chain rule is unchanged, there's just one extra ascent trip.

e5e14802686b.zh: KP-14：兩次反傳太貴，才會有 SWP、SDS、ASAM 這些加速與尺度修正。
e5e14802686b.en: KP-14: two backward passes are too expensive, which is why speedups and scale fixes like SWP, SDS, and ASAM exist.

4a23a29c8b95.zh: Vanilla SAM 一句話重講：在半徑 $\rho$ 的球裡先走到損失最高的鄰居（$p=2$ 時就是沿梯度走長度 $\rho$ 的 $\boldsymbol{\epsilon}^*$），再在那一點算梯度來更新 $\boldsymbol{w}$，等於同時壓低訓練損失與銳度，逼解落在平坦谷。
4a23a29c8b95.en: Vanilla SAM in one sentence: inside a ball of radius $\rho$, first walk to the neighbor with the highest loss (for $p=2$, that is the $\boldsymbol{\epsilon}^*$ of length $\rho$ along the gradient), then compute the gradient at that point to update $\boldsymbol{w}$; this lowers the training loss and the sharpness at the same time, forcing the solution into a flat valley.

c777cf4b9cff.zh: 「先摸最慘鄰居，再下山；$\boldsymbol{\epsilon}^*=\rho\cdot\mathrm{grad}/\|\mathrm{grad}\|$，梯度要在擾動點算。」
c777cf4b9cff.en: "Feel out the worst neighbor first, then go downhill; $\boldsymbol{\epsilon}^*=\rho\cdot\mathrm{grad}/\|\mathrm{grad}\|$, and the gradient is computed at the perturbed point."

e11b58686cfd.zh: 教授祕笈：ESAM 與 ASAM——遮罩與只挑銳樣本
e11b58686cfd.en: Professor's Secret Notes: ESAM and ASAM, masks and picking only the sharp samples

36f10358da46.zh: 主線比喻是「驗屋師傅的兩把省力尺：遮罩抽檢、只驗漏水戶」。KP-13 的 Vanilla SAM 每間房子的每面牆都敲兩遍（兩次反向傳播），工時大約是普通 SGD 的兩倍。Efficient SAM（ESAM）請師傅改用兩招偷懶但不偷工：SWP 是隨機遮罩，只敲一部分牆再按比例放大；SDS 是先輕敲一遍，只對「真的漏水」的樣本做完整 SAM。另外，尺如果不管房子實際大小、永遠用同一把 $\rho$，量出來的銳度會被權重尺度唬弄——Adaptive SAM（ASAM）就是讓尺跟著房子縮放，sharpness 才具尺度不變性。
36f10358da46.en: The main analogy is "the home inspector's two labor-saving rulers: spot-checking with a mask, and inspecting only the leaky units". KP-13's Vanilla SAM knocks on every wall of every house twice (two backpropagation passes), taking about twice the labor of plain SGD. Efficient SAM (ESAM) has the inspector use two tricks that cut effort without cutting corners: SWP is a random mask that knocks on only some of the walls and then scales up proportionally; SDS taps everything lightly once first and does the full SAM only on samples that "really leak". Also, if the ruler ignores the actual size of the house and always uses the same $\rho$, the measured sharpness gets fooled by the weight scale; Adaptive SAM (ASAM) makes the ruler scale with the house, so that the sharpness is scale-invariant.

5f98cd79e176.zh: 先講白話：Vanilla SAM 正確但貴；ESAM 用「少敲幾面牆、少驗幾戶」把成本降下來，ASAM 則修正「同一間屋換個單位制、銳度數字就不一樣」的毛病。
5f98cd79e176.en: In plain words first: Vanilla SAM is correct but expensive; ESAM brings the cost down by "knocking on fewer walls and inspecting fewer units", and ASAM fixes the flaw that "the same house measured in a different unit system gives a different sharpness number".

d1b8ca29d4e5.zh: 為什麼需要它們？權重有 $n$ 維、一個 mini-batch 有一堆樣本，兩次反傳乘上全維度、全批次，訓練大型網路會痛。SWP 省的是權重維度，SDS 省的是資料維度，ASAM 解的是尺度敏感，三件事不要攪成一鍋。
d1b8ca29d4e5.en: Why do we need them? The weights have $n$ dimensions and a mini-batch holds a pile of samples; two backward passes times all dimensions and the whole batch hurts when training large networks. SWP saves along the weight dimension, SDS saves along the data dimension, and ASAM solves scale sensitivity; don't stir these three things into one pot.

b096d06f868a.zh: SWP（Stochastic Weight Perturbation，隨機權重擾動）。每步抽一個二元遮罩 $\boldsymbol{m}=(m_1,\ldots,m_n)^{\top}$，每個 $m_i$ 獨立來自 Bernoulli$(\beta)$——以機率 $\beta$ 選中第 $i$ 個權重去擾動。近似（式 54；分量是逐元相乘，再除以 $\beta$ 把被丟掉的機率補回來）：
b096d06f868a.en: SWP (Stochastic Weight Perturbation). At each step, draw a binary mask $\boldsymbol{m}=(m_1,\ldots,m_n)^{\top}$, where each $m_i$ comes independently from Bernoulli$(\beta)$: the $i$-th weight is selected for perturbation with probability $\beta$. The approximation (Eq. 54; the components are multiplied element-wise, then divided by $\beta$ to make up for the probability of being dropped):

3d01217096b9.zh: 關鍵性質：$\mathbb{E}[m_i]=\beta$ 且 $m_i$ 與 $\boldsymbol{\epsilon}^*$ 獨立，所以
3d01217096b9.en: Key property: $\mathbb{E}[m_i]=\beta$ and $m_i$ is independent of $\boldsymbol{\epsilon}^*$, so

c7d8d810ef7b.zh: 期望上跟完整 SAM 一樣，只是每步只算子集。
c7d8d810ef7b.en: In expectation it is the same as full SAM; it just computes a subset at each step.

ec0baa0cdd7c.zh: SDS（Sharpness-sensitive Data Selection，銳度敏感資料挑選）。不是整個 mini-batch $\mathcal{B}$ 都走第二次反傳，只留擾動後損失漲太多的樣本（式 55）：
ec0baa0cdd7c.en: SDS (Sharpness-sensitive Data Selection). Instead of sending the whole mini-batch $\mathcal{B}$ through the second backward pass, keep only the samples whose loss rises too much after the perturbation (Eq. 55):

e64217b753c4.zh: $\alpha\gt 0$ 是閾值；$\mathcal{B}^{+}$ 是銳樣本，$\mathcal{B}^{-}$ 是漲幅不夠的鈍樣本。SAM 的第二趟損失與梯度只在 $\mathcal{B}^{+}$ 上算。
e64217b753c4.en: $\alpha\gt 0$ is the threshold; $\mathcal{B}^{+}$ are the sharp samples, and $\mathcal{B}^{-}$ are the blunt samples whose increase isn't large enough. SAM's second-pass loss and gradient are computed only on $\mathcal{B}^{+}$.

8c4b0d08515a.zh: ASAM（Adaptive SAM）。Vanilla 用固定 $\|\boldsymbol{\epsilon}\|_p\leq\rho$。若把權重用可逆矩陣 $\boldsymbol{A}$ 做重新縮放，同一個解的銳度數字會變。ASAM 引入正規化算子 $T_{\boldsymbol{w}}^{-1}$，滿足 $T_{\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{w}}^{-1}\boldsymbol{A}=T_{\boldsymbol{w}}^{-1}$（式 56），改優化（式 57）：
8c4b0d08515a.en: ASAM (Adaptive SAM). Vanilla uses a fixed $\|\boldsymbol{\epsilon}\|_p\leq\rho$. If the weights are re-scaled with an invertible matrix $\boldsymbol{A}$, the sharpness number of the same solution changes. ASAM introduces a normalization operator $T_{\boldsymbol{w}}^{-1}$ satisfying $T_{\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{w}}^{-1}\boldsymbol{A}=T_{\boldsymbol{w}}^{-1}$ (Eq. 56), and optimizes instead (Eq. 57):

7d09e3cab2ce.zh: 約束從「擾動本身的長度」改成「經 $T_{\boldsymbol{w}}^{-1}$ 正規化後的長度」，sharpness 對權重尺度不變。
7d09e3cab2ce.en: The constraint changes from "the length of the perturbation itself" to "the length after normalization by $T_{\boldsymbol{w}}^{-1}$", so the sharpness is invariant to the weight scale.

0a3da17ebe9d.zh: 數值真的算一遍：遮罩、銳樣本、尺度尺
0a3da17ebe9d.en: Actually computing the numbers: masks, sharp samples, the scaling ruler

9583d86a394a.zh: 接 KP-13 的 $\boldsymbol{\epsilon}^{*}=(0.06,0.08,0.10,0.12)$（四個權重），取 $\beta=0.5$，這一抽的遮罩 $\boldsymbol{m}=(1,0,1,0)$——只敲第 1、第 3 面牆。SWP 擾動：
9583d86a394a.en: Continuing from KP-13 with $\boldsymbol{\epsilon}^{*}=(0.06,0.08,0.10,0.12)$ (four weights), take $\beta=0.5$; this draw's mask is $\boldsymbol{m}=(1,0,1,0)$, so only the 1st and 3rd walls get knocked. The SWP perturbation:

2841fae5a928.zh: 被選中的分量乘 $2$、沒選中的變 $0$。長期下來，因為選中機率正好是 $1/2$，期望仍回到 $(0.06,0.08,0.10,0.12)$。
2841fae5a928.en: Selected components are multiplied by $2$, unselected ones become $0$. In the long run, because the selection probability is exactly $1/2$, the expectation still comes back to $(0.06,0.08,0.10,0.12)$.

ad86a9e3b83a.zh: 同一 mini-batch 四筆樣本，擾動前後損失差與 $\alpha=0.10$：
ad86a9e3b83a.en: Four samples in the same mini-batch, the loss difference before and after perturbation, and $\alpha=0.10$:

8433d8794d29.zh: 第二次反傳只打 2、4 兩筆，資料成本砍半。師傅的邏輯很生活：漏水的戶才值得做完整驗屋，本來就不漏的敲了也是浪費工。
8433d8794d29.en: The second backward pass only hits samples 2 and 4, cutting the data cost in half. The inspector's logic is everyday common sense: only the leaky units are worth a full inspection; knocking on the ones that never leaked is wasted labor.

ff232f18efa1.zh: ASAM 用一維函數看尺度。令 $\mathcal{L}(w)=(w-2)^{2}$，在谷底 $w=2$ 處 $\mathcal{L}=0$。Vanilla 取 $| \varepsilon |\leq\rho=0.1$，銳度 $=0.1^{2}=0.01$。把參數改寫成 $\tilde{w}=w/2$（同一個函數變成 $\tilde{\mathcal{L}}(\tilde{w})=4(\tilde{w}-1)^{2}$），在對應點 $\tilde{w}=1$ 再用同一個 $\rho=0.1$，銳度變成 $4\times 0.01=0.04$——屋沒變，尺讀數卻跳了四倍。若 $T_{w}=|w|$，ASAM 允許 $|\varepsilon|\leq\rho|w|$：在 $w=2$ 可擾 $0.2$，銳度 $0.04$；在 $\tilde{w}=1$ 可擾 $0.1$，銳度也是 $0.04$。尺跟著房子縮，數字才比得了。
ff232f18efa1.en: ASAM: look at scale with a one-dimensional function. Let $\mathcal{L}(w)=(w-2)^{2}$; at the valley floor $w=2$, $\mathcal{L}=0$. Vanilla takes $| \varepsilon |\leq\rho=0.1$, sharpness $=0.1^{2}=0.01$. Rewrite the parameter as $\tilde{w}=w/2$ (the same function becomes $\tilde{\mathcal{L}}(\tilde{w})=4(\tilde{w}-1)^{2}$); at the corresponding point $\tilde{w}=1$, with the same $\rho=0.1$, the sharpness becomes $4\times 0.01=0.04$: the house hasn't changed, but the ruler's reading jumped fourfold. If $T_{w}=|w|$, ASAM allows $|\varepsilon|\leq\rho|w|$: at $w=2$ the perturbation can be $0.2$, sharpness $0.04$; at $\tilde{w}=1$ it can be $0.1$, sharpness also $0.04$. Only when the ruler scales with the house can the numbers be compared.

b52cd5f14bd7.zh: 你大概會覺得：「隨機丟掉一半權重、再丟掉一半樣本，這不就變粗糙了嗎？」反轉在於：SWP 不是亂丟，是無偏抽樣——乘 $1/\beta$ 正是為了讓期望對得上完整 $\boldsymbol{\epsilon}^*$；SDS 也不是隨機丟資料，是把預算花在「真的尖」的樣本上。真正會讓銳度失真的，反而是你以為最無害的那件事：把權重整體放大縮小。Vanilla 的固定 $\rho$ 球會被尺度愚弄，ASAM 才對症。
b52cd5f14bd7.en: You're probably thinking: "Randomly drop half the weights, then drop half the samples; doesn't that just make it crude?" The twist: SWP doesn't drop things at random; it's unbiased sampling. Multiplying by $1/\beta$ is exactly what makes the expectation match the full $\boldsymbol{\epsilon}^*$. SDS doesn't drop data at random either; it spends the budget on the samples that are "really sharp". What actually distorts the sharpness is the thing you'd think is most harmless: scaling all the weights up or down. Vanilla's fixed $\rho$-ball gets fooled by the scale, and ASAM is the right cure.

beeae75121fc.zh: 把驗屋換成工廠抽檢：一千顆螺絲不必顆顆用扭力板手（Vanilla），可以隨機抽 $\beta$ 比例再加權還原（SWP），也可以先用聽音篩出「共振異常」的才做全檢（SDS）；量測公差還得依螺絲直徑自動調整（ASAM）。換一組數自己算：$\beta=0.25$，$\boldsymbol{\epsilon}^{*}=(0.8,0.4)$，$\boldsymbol{m}=(0,1)$，寫出 $\widehat{\boldsymbol{\epsilon}}$；並說明為什麼 $\mathbb{E}[\widehat{\epsilon}_{2}]$ 仍應等於 $0.4$。
beeae75121fc.en: Swap the home inspection for factory spot checks: a thousand screws don't each need a torque wrench (Vanilla); you can randomly sample a fraction $\beta$ and reweight to recover the total (SWP), or first screen by sound for the ones with "abnormal resonance" and only fully inspect those (SDS); and the measurement tolerance also has to adjust automatically to the screw's diameter (ASAM). Compute it yourself with new numbers: $\beta=0.25$, $\boldsymbol{\epsilon}^{*}=(0.8,0.4)$, $\boldsymbol{m}=(0,1)$; write down $\widehat{\boldsymbol{\epsilon}}$, and explain why $\mathbb{E}[\widehat{\epsilon}_{2}]$ should still equal $0.4$.

ff60f7a3c9d3.zh: 誤解「SWP 的遮罩是高斯雜訊」。$m_i$ 是 Bernoulli$(\beta)$ 的 $0/1$，不是 $U(0,1)$ 也不是高斯。
ff60f7a3c9d3.en: Misconception: "SWP's mask is Gaussian noise." $m_i$ is a $0/1$ from Bernoulli$(\beta)$, neither $U(0,1)$ nor Gaussian.

75bdb1a93025.zh: 誤解「SDS 的 $\mathcal{B}^{+}$ 是損失最低或驗證集」。定義是擾動後損失增量大於 $\alpha$，跟「好不好分」不是同一件事。
75bdb1a93025.en: Misconception: "SDS's $\mathcal{B}^{+}$ is the lowest-loss samples, or the validation set." The definition is the loss increase after perturbation is greater than $\alpha$, which is not the same thing as "easy or hard to classify".

d3c5e8119464.zh: 誤解「ASAM 少做一次反傳、或取消了 min-max」。它改的是擾動球的形狀（尺度不變），不是把 SAM 變回普通 SGD。
d3c5e8119464.en: Misconception: "ASAM does one fewer backward pass, or removes the min-max." What it changes is the shape of the perturbation ball (scale invariance); it doesn't turn SAM back into plain SGD.

dfe361404cc2.zh: 誤解「$\beta$ 越小越好」。$\beta$ 太小，單步變異大，期望無偏不代表每一步都準。
dfe361404cc2.en: Misconception: "the smaller $\beta$, the better." If $\beta$ is too small, the per-step variance is large; being unbiased in expectation doesn't mean every step is accurate.

41c3551dcd65.zh: KP-13：Vanilla SAM 的 $\boldsymbol{\epsilon}^*$ 與兩次反傳；本節是同一具引擎的省油與校準套件。
41c3551dcd65.en: KP-13: Vanilla SAM's $\boldsymbol{\epsilon}^*$ and its two backward passes; this section is the fuel-saving and calibration kit for the same engine.

0cb5ead87b54.zh: KP-8：SDS 作用在 mini-batch 上，先有 $\mathcal{B}$ 才切得出 $\mathcal{B}^{+}$。
0cb5ead87b54.en: KP-8: SDS acts on the mini-batch; you need $\mathcal{B}$ before you can carve out $\mathcal{B}^{+}$.

10413872a8c3.zh: KP-7：ESAM 仍是隨機梯度家族，只是梯度來自擾動點與子集。
10413872a8c3.en: KP-7: ESAM is still in the stochastic gradient family; the gradient just comes from the perturbed point and a subset.

2028fa1008ec.zh: KP-12：大家都在追平坦極小值；ASAM 提醒你「平坦」的數字會被參數尺度汙染。
2028fa1008ec.en: KP-12: everyone is chasing flat minima; ASAM reminds you that the number for "flat" gets contaminated by the parameter scale.

546b7f9d4b43.zh: ESAM 與 ASAM 一句話重講：SWP 用 Bernoulli 遮罩只擾一部分權重並除以 $\beta$ 保持期望無偏，SDS 只對損失漲幅超過 $\alpha$ 的銳樣本做 SAM，ASAM 把 $\|\boldsymbol{\epsilon}\|\leq\rho$ 改成 $\|T_{\boldsymbol{w}}^{-1}\boldsymbol{\epsilon}\|\leq\rho$ 讓銳度不隨權重縮放而變——三招分別砍維度成本、砍資料成本、校正尺。
546b7f9d4b43.en: ESAM and ASAM in one sentence: SWP uses a Bernoulli mask to perturb only some of the weights and divides by $\beta$ to keep the expectation unbiased, SDS runs SAM only on the sharp samples whose loss rises by more than $\alpha$, and ASAM changes $\|\boldsymbol{\epsilon}\|\leq\rho$ to $\|T_{\boldsymbol{w}}^{-1}\boldsymbol{\epsilon}\|\leq\rho$ so that the sharpness doesn't change with weight scaling. The three tricks cut the dimension cost, cut the data cost, and calibrate the ruler, respectively.

ebc5912ee664.zh: 「遮罩抽牆補 $1/\beta$，銳樣本才驗第二遍；尺要跟著權重縮，否則銳度被尺度騙。」
ebc5912ee664.en: "Mask the walls and make up $1/\beta$; only sharp samples get the second pass; the ruler must scale with the weights, or the scale fools the sharpness."

c8777e6e136a.zh: 教授祕笈：過參數化收斂——坑幾乎一樣深
c8777e6e136a.en: Professor's Secret Notes: overparameterized convergence — the pits are almost equally deep

3f6034291ca7.zh: 主線比喻是「礦區裡的坑幾乎一樣深」。古典統計學說：參數比資料多，模型會過擬合，你掉進哪個坑、坑有多深，全看運氣。深度學習最刺眼的現象卻是：網路嚴重過參數化（可學參數遠多於訓練樣本），訓練不僅經常成功，不同初始化掉進的那些局部極小值，在訓練損失上看起來幾乎一樣好——像整片礦區的坑深度都差不多，沒有「看起來像谷、其實是個淺窪地」的假坑（spurious local minima）。Proposition 4、5 與 Fig. 7 要講的，就是這幅礦區圖為什麼在理論上說得通；它們保證的是訓練損失能被挖到底，不是測試泛化。
3f6034291ca7.en: The main metaphor is "the pits in the mining field are almost equally deep". Classical statistics says: with more parameters than data, the model will overfit, and which pit you fall into and how deep it is comes down to luck. Yet the most glaring phenomenon in deep learning is this: networks are heavily overparameterized (far more learnable parameters than training samples), and not only does training often succeed, the local minima that different initializations fall into all look almost equally good in training loss — as if every pit in the whole mining field had about the same depth, with no false pits that "look like a valley but are really a shallow puddle" (spurious local minima). What Proposition 4, Proposition 5 and Fig. 7 explain is why this picture of the mining field makes sense theoretically; what they guarantee is that the training loss can be dug all the way down, not test generalization.

71e75fef61fb.zh: 先講白話：參數多到離譜，梯度法面對非凸損失，居然還能收到全域或近全域極小值。 過參數化可以來自「寬」（每層神經元多）、「深」（層數多）、或兩者都有。非凸通常意味著到處是鞍點與假谷，實務上卻很少卡死——這兩條命題就是在適當假設下，把「為什麼通常能成功」寫嚴謹。
71e75fef61fb.en: First, in plain words: with an absurd number of parameters, gradient methods facing a non-convex loss still manage to converge to a global or near-global minimum. Overparameterization can come from being "wide" (many neurons per layer), "deep" (many layers), or both. Non-convex usually means saddle points and false valleys everywhere, yet in practice training rarely gets stuck for good — these two propositions make "why it usually succeeds" rigorous under suitable assumptions.

ff89469c2ecf.zh: 為什麼需要它？前面整章都在教你怎麼走（GD、SGD、Adam、SAM），還沒回答「這片地本身會不會把你困住」。本節把優化從「演算法技巧」接到「損失曲面的形狀」。
ff89469c2ecf.en: Why do we need this? The whole chapter so far has taught you how to walk (GD, SGD, Adam, SAM), but has not answered "will the terrain itself trap you?". This section connects optimization from "algorithmic tricks" to "the shape of the loss surface".

d2703587c6ba.en: The symbols, one by one (Prop 4, Prop 5, Eqs. 58–59)

6bf1c3357bf8.zh: Proposition 4（淺層、一隱藏層）：映射 $\boldsymbol{x}\mapsto \boldsymbol{v}^{\top}\sigma(\boldsymbol{W}\boldsymbol{x})$，$\boldsymbol{W}\in\mathbb{R}^{k\times d}$，$\boldsymbol{v}\in\mathbb{R}^{k}$，損失是 MSE
6bf1c3357bf8.en: Proposition 4 (shallow, one hidden layer): the mapping $\boldsymbol{x}\mapsto \boldsymbol{v}^{\top}\sigma(\boldsymbol{W}\boldsymbol{x})$, $\boldsymbol{W}\in\mathbb{R}^{k\times d}$, $\boldsymbol{v}\in\mathbb{R}^{k}$, and the loss is MSE

f01d2ab1dfc2.zh: 條件：激活 $\sigma(z)=z^{2}$（二次）、寬度 $k\geq 2d$、輸出層 $\boldsymbol{v}$ 至少有 $d$ 個正、$d$ 個負。則三件事成立：
f01d2ab1dfc2.en: Conditions: activation $\sigma(z)=z^{2}$ (quadratic), width $k\geq 2d$, and the output layer $\boldsymbol{v}$ has at least $d$ positive and $d$ negative entries. Then three things hold:

aedc4cd9fbd0.zh: 無 spurious local minima：所有局部極小值都是全域極小值——沒有「梯度為零但比全域差一截」的假坑。
aedc4cd9fbd0.en: No spurious local minima: every local minimum is a global minimum — there are no false pits with "zero gradient but noticeably worse than the global one".

7a0abcf9ff85.zh: 鞍點有逃逸方向：任一鞍點 $\boldsymbol{W}_s$ 存在方向 $\boldsymbol{U}$，使 $\mathrm{vec}(\boldsymbol{U})^{\top}\nabla^{2}\mathcal{L}(\boldsymbol{W}_s)\,\mathrm{vec}(\boldsymbol{U})\lt 0$——Hessian 有嚴格負曲率，一階法可以被推走。
7a0abcf9ff85.en: Saddle points have an escape direction: for any saddle point $\boldsymbol{W}_s$ there exists a direction $\boldsymbol{U}$ such that $\mathrm{vec}(\boldsymbol{U})^{\top}\nabla^{2}\mathcal{L}(\boldsymbol{W}_s)\,\mathrm{vec}(\boldsymbol{U})\lt 0$ — the Hessian has strictly negative curvature, so first-order methods can be pushed away.

f6c5b0a2d7e4.zh: 零訓練損失可達：若 $d\leq n\leq c d^{2}$（$c\gt 0$ 常數），全域最優可以完美擬合訓練資料。
f6c5b0a2d7e4.en: Zero training loss is attainable: if $d\leq n\leq c d^{2}$ ($c\gt 0$ a constant), the global optimum can fit the training data perfectly.

cc06fb0007d5.zh: Fig. 7 的畫面就是：幾乎所有局部解都夠好、等同全域解；不同初始化在訓練集上表現相近。
cc06fb0007d5.en: The picture in Fig. 7 is exactly this: almost all local solutions are good enough and equivalent to the global solution; different initializations perform similarly on the training set.

4bcf10c9389b.zh: Proposition 5（深層、ReLU、MSE）：$l$ 層全連接，資料已正規化（$\|\boldsymbol{x}_i\|_2=1$，最後一維 $1/\sqrt{2}$），任兩筆訓練樣本距離 $\|\boldsymbol{x}_i-\boldsymbol{x}_j\|_2\geq\delta\gt 0$，權重隨機初始化。寬度 $m$ 夠大時：
4bcf10c9389b.en: Proposition 5 (deep, ReLU, MSE): $l$ fully connected layers, the data are normalized ($\|\boldsymbol{x}_i\|_2=1$, last dimension $1/\sqrt{2}$), any two training samples are at distance $\|\boldsymbol{x}_i-\boldsymbol{x}_j\|_2\geq\delta\gt 0$, and the weights are randomly initialized. When the width $m$ is large enough:

32c8f1d4a815.zh: 全批次 GD：寬度 $m\geq\Omega(\mathrm{poly}(n,l,\delta^{-1})d)$、學習率 $\eta=\Theta(d\delta/(\mathrm{poly}(n,l)m))$，則約
32c8f1d4a815.en: Full-batch GD: with width $m\geq\Omega(\mathrm{poly}(n,l,\delta^{-1})d)$ and learning rate $\eta=\Theta(d\delta/(\mathrm{poly}(n,l)m))$, then after about

258ca614e2b0.zh: 步後，以高機率 $1-e^{-\Omega(\log^{2} m)}$ 把損失降到 $\lt \epsilon$。
258ca614e2b0.en: steps, the loss is brought down to $\lt \epsilon$ with high probability $1-e^{-\Omega(\log^{2} m)}$.

85f4d2608f0b.zh: Mini-batch SGD（batch 大小 $b$）：寬度還要再除以 $b$ 的量級，步數（式 59）多一個 $\log^{2} m / b$ 因子，同樣高機率收斂到 $\lt \epsilon$。
85f4d2608f0b.en: Mini-batch SGD (batch size $b$): the width requirement is further divided by a factor of order $b$, the number of steps (Eq. 59) gains an extra $\log^{2} m / b$ factor, and it likewise converges to $\lt \epsilon$ with high probability.

636e2439ae2e.zh: 重點結構：對 $\epsilon$ 只是對數依賴（要更精只要多走一點），對資料分離 $\delta$ 是 $1/\delta^{2}$（兩筆樣本太像，礦坑邊界糊掉，就要走更久）。
636e2439ae2e.en: The key structure: the dependence on $\epsilon$ is only logarithmic (to get more precise you just walk a bit longer), while the dependence on the data separation $\delta$ is $1/\delta^{2}$ (if two samples are too alike, the boundaries between pits blur and you have to walk much longer).

c474a2cba8eb.zh: 數值真的算一遍：淺層條件與深層步數量級
c474a2cba8eb.en: Actually crunching the numbers: the shallow-network conditions and the order of the deep-network step count

addeda517afd.zh: 先看 Prop 4 的門檻。輸入維度 $d=2$，則隱藏層至少 $k\geq 4$，輸出層 $\boldsymbol{v}$ 至少兩個正、兩個負。訓練樣本數要落在 $2\leq n\leq c\cdot 4$；取 $c=3$，則 $n\leq 12$ 時理論保證可以走到零損失。例如 $n=8$、$k=4$：參數個數約 $k\cdot d+k=12$，已經不少於樣本數 8——典型的過參數化，命題卻說假坑不存在、鞍點可逃、訓練可完美擬合。
addeda517afd.en: First, the thresholds of Prop 4. With input dimension $d=2$, the hidden layer needs at least $k\geq 4$, and the output layer $\boldsymbol{v}$ needs at least two positive and two negative entries. The number of training samples must fall in $2\leq n\leq c\cdot 4$; taking $c=3$, the theory guarantees we can reach zero loss when $n\leq 12$. For example, with $n=8$ and $k=4$: the number of parameters is about $k\cdot d+k=12$, already no fewer than the 8 samples — a typical case of overparameterization, yet the proposition says false pits do not exist, saddle points can be escaped, and training can fit perfectly.

e5e2f0830d9b.zh: 再看「坑幾乎一樣深」的數字直覺。兩次隨機初始化，訓練損失分別收到 $1.2\times 10^{-3}$ 與 $9\times 10^{-4}$，差在小數點後第四位；古典想像裡，其中一次本該卡在損失 $2.5$ 的假谷。Fig. 7 要你記住的是這張表，不是某一條曲線的造型：
e5e2f0830d9b.en: Next, the numerical intuition behind "the pits are almost equally deep". Two random initializations converge to training losses of $1.2\times 10^{-3}$ and $9\times 10^{-4}$ respectively, differing only in the fourth decimal place; in the classical picture, one of them should have got stuck in a false valley with loss $2.5$. What Fig. 7 wants you to remember is this table, not the shape of any particular curve:

e765c6488cfc.zh: 可能卡在很差的局部解
e765c6488cfc.en: May get stuck in a very poor local solution

00fcc32be668.zh: 訓練損失與種子 B 同量級，近全域
00fcc32be668.en: Training loss of the same order as seed B, near-global

523a63546cfa.en: Reaches the global one only with luck

1e00974b8a7a.zh: 同樣近全域；坑深幾乎一樣
1e00974b8a7a.en: Likewise near-global; the pits are almost equally deep

294d595d873d.zh: Prop 5 的 $T$ 原文沒給 $\mathrm{poly}$ 的具體係數，下面用示意 $\mathrm{poly}(n,l)=n^{2}l$ 只示範「對數 vs 平方」誰比較痛。取 $n=100$、$l=3$，則 $n^{2}l=30000$。
294d595d873d.en: The original text does not give the concrete coefficients of the $\mathrm{poly}$ in Prop 5's $T$, so below we use the illustrative $\mathrm{poly}(n,l)=n^{2}l$ just to show which hurts more, "logarithmic vs. squared". Take $n=100$ and $l=3$; then $n^{2}l=30000$.

bacb9bdcd6b1.zh: 要更精（A→B）幾乎只多付對數帳單；資料擠在一起（A→C）則按 $1/\delta^{2}$ 漲——分離度比「再多幾個零」貴得多。
bacb9bdcd6b1.en: Getting more precise (A→B) costs you little more than a logarithmic bill; data crammed together (A→C) grows as $1/\delta^{2}$ — separation is far more expensive than "a few more zeros".

2b2e620069e3.zh: 開場那句「參數比資料多應該過擬合」仍然在你腦海的話，這裡就是翻盤的地方：這些命題把「訓練可以成功」從玄學變成定理，但它們沒有順便把泛化也證完。 零訓練損失只說明礦坑夠深、挖得到底；換一座山（測試集）坑還在不在，原文自己說那是另一個問題。所以你若看到「過參數化所以泛化好」，那是把 Prop 4/5 讀過頭了——本章理論的射程停在優化。
2b2e620069e3.en: If the opening line "more parameters than data should overfit" is still in your head, this is where the tables turn: these propositions turn "training can succeed" from mysticism into a theorem, but they do not prove generalization along the way. Zero training loss only says the pits are deep enough and you can dig to the bottom; whether the pits are still there on a different mountain (the test set), the original text itself says, is a separate question. So if you see "overparameterized, therefore it generalizes well", that is reading too much into Prop 4/5 — the reach of this chapter's theory stops at optimization.

c317413a5ddf.zh: 把礦區換成大型樂團：樂手（參數）比曲子小節（樣本）還多，照理該亂成一團；若編制夠寬、聲部正負成對（對應 $k\geq 2d$ 與 $\boldsymbol{v}$ 的正負），命題說沒有「聽起來像完成、其實差一個八度」的假結局，卡關的只是鞍點，一推就走。換成數字練習：$\delta$ 從 $0.5$ 降到 $0.25$，式 (58) 的 $T$ 量級會變成幾倍？不要算 $\mathrm{poly}$，只看 $\delta^{-2}$。
c317413a5ddf.en: Swap the mining field for a big orchestra: there are more musicians (parameters) than bars in the piece (samples), so by rights it should be chaos; but if the ensemble is wide enough and the voices come in positive/negative pairs (matching $k\geq 2d$ and the signs of $\boldsymbol{v}$), the proposition says there is no false ending that "sounds finished but is actually an octave off" — the only places you get stuck are saddle points, and one push gets you moving. Now as a numerical exercise: if $\delta$ drops from $0.5$ to $0.25$, by what factor does the order of $T$ in Eq. (58) change? Don't compute the $\mathrm{poly}$; look only at $\delta^{-2}$.

79c909bba375.zh: 誤解「無 spurious local minima」＝「沒有任何局部極小值」。意思是局部即全域，不是沒有極小值。
79c909bba375.en: Misconception: "no spurious local minima" = "no local minima at all". It means local is global, not that there are no minima.

3f3c1ac9b618.zh: 誤解「有鞍點就一定卡死」。第二點說鞍點有嚴格負曲率，隨機初始化下 GD 通常逃得掉，不必一上來就上二階法。
3f3c1ac9b618.en: Misconception: "if there are saddle points, you will definitely get stuck". Item 2 says saddle points have strictly negative curvature, so with random initialization GD can usually escape; there is no need to jump straight to second-order methods.

efcfcc7ef3db.zh: 誤解「Prop 5 保證測試誤差 $\lt \epsilon$」。$\epsilon$ 是訓練損失；式 (58)(59) 的 $T$ 是把訓練損失壓下去的步數。
efcfcc7ef3db.en: Misconception: "Prop 5 guarantees test error $\lt \epsilon$". $\epsilon$ is the training loss; the $T$ in Eqs. (58)(59) is the number of steps to push the training loss down.

c19c795bc07d.zh: 誤解「寬度隨便一點就好」。$m$ 必須大到 $\mathrm{poly}(n,l,1/\delta)$ 那個量級，條件沒滿足時定理不保。
c19c795bc07d.en: Misconception: "any width will do". $m$ must be as large as the order of $\mathrm{poly}(n,l,1/\delta)$; if the condition is not met, the theorem does not guarantee anything.

83ef69b6636e.zh: KP-12、KP-13：SAM 在「很多谷裡選平坦的」；本節先保證「這些谷的訓練深度差不多」，平坦是下一層的選擇，不是「有沒有谷」的問題。
83ef69b6636e.en: KP-12, KP-13: SAM is about "choosing the flat one among many valleys"; this section first guarantees that "these valleys have about the same training depth". Flatness is the next level of choice, not a question of "whether there is a valley".

0491d49de1c1.zh: KP-2、KP-7：一階法（GD / SGD）在這張曲面上夠用，呼應鞍點可逃。
0491d49de1c1.en: KP-2, KP-7: first-order methods (GD / SGD) are good enough on this surface, echoing the fact that saddle points can be escaped.

1e8e70bace5f.zh: KP-9：那時比較 $O(1/t)$ 與 SGD 的鄰域停滯；這裡是過參數化深度網的多項式時間保證，問題從「步長策略」換成「曲面會不會困人」。
1e8e70bace5f.en: KP-9: there we compared $O(1/t)$ with SGD's neighborhood stalling; here it is a polynomial-time guarantee for overparameterized deep networks, and the question shifts from "step-size strategy" to "will the surface trap you".

c605c0e0849d.zh: KP-16：會把「優化成功」與「泛化未解」拆開，當全章收網的最後一錘。
c605c0e0849d.en: KP-16: will separate "optimization succeeds" from "generalization is unsolved", as the final hammer blow that wraps up the whole chapter.

7fab3990858e.zh: 過參數化收斂一句話重講：淺層二次網在夠寬、輸出正負成對時沒有假坑、鞍點可逃、樣本不太多時可零訓練損失；深層 ReLU 在夠寬、資料有最小間隔 $\delta$ 時，GD/SGD 能在 $\mathrm{poly}(n,l)\log(1/\epsilon)/\delta^{2}$ 量級的步數把訓練損失壓到任意小——礦坑幾乎一樣深，但換山能不能走是另一題。
7fab3990858e.en: Overparameterized convergence restated in one sentence: a shallow quadratic network that is wide enough, with output weights in positive/negative pairs, has no false pits, its saddle points can be escaped, and with not too many samples it can reach zero training loss; a deep ReLU network that is wide enough, with data at a minimum separation $\delta$, can have its training loss pushed arbitrarily low by GD/SGD in a number of steps of order $\mathrm{poly}(n,l)\log(1/\epsilon)/\delta^{2}$ — the pits are almost equally deep, but whether you can still walk on a different mountain is another question.

26342bc97c6f.zh: 「參數再多，假坑消失、鞍點可逃；訓練能挖到底，不代表測試也是同一口井。」
26342bc97c6f.en: "However many parameters you add, the false pits vanish and the saddle points can be escaped; being able to dig to the bottom in training doesn't mean the test is the same well."

76ac5a13401e.zh: 教授祕笈：全章收網——能訓成功≠已懂泛化
76ac5a13401e.en: Professor's Secret Notes: wrapping up the chapter — training successfully ≠ understanding generalization

36ed0f0a35e1.zh: 主線比喻是「這台器材練到沒阻力，不代表換健身房還能舉」。整章教你怎麼在高維非凸曲面上把訓練損失往下推：梯度怎麼走、反傳怎麼算、SGD 怎麼省、Adam 怎麼調步、SAM 怎麼找平坦谷、過參數化為什麼通常挖得到底。§7.3 告訴你文獻還把同樣的故事寫到 ReLU、ResNet、代數幾何；§8 把工具鏈收成一條線。最後那句話務必帶走：能把訓練這台器材的重量歸零，不表示你已經懂為什麼換一批測試資料還能表現好。 能訓成功≠已懂泛化。
36ed0f0a35e1.en: The main metaphor is "training on this machine until it feels effortless doesn't mean you can still lift at a different gym". The whole chapter taught you how to push the training loss down on a high-dimensional non-convex surface: how the gradient walks, how backprop computes it, how SGD saves cost, how Adam tunes the step, how SAM finds flat valleys, and why overparameterization usually lets you dig to the bottom. §7.3 tells you the literature has extended the same story to ReLU, ResNet and algebraic geometry; §8 gathers the toolchain into one line. Make sure you take the last sentence with you: being able to bring the weight on this training machine down to zero does not mean you understand why you still perform well on a new batch of test data. Training successfully ≠ understanding generalization.

8deb24c48f4c.zh: 先講白話：本章是「訓練怎麼算得起來、走得下去」的工具箱，不是「為什麼測起來也準」的完整答案。 §7.1–7.2 的命題只是冰山一角；§7.3 用不同激活、不同架構、不同數學工具把「一階法不是盲目碰運氣」補成一幅更密的網，但網的邊界仍停在收斂與訓練損失。
8deb24c48f4c.en: First, in plain words: this chapter is a toolbox for "how training becomes computable and keeps moving", not the complete answer to "why it also tests accurately". The propositions in §7.1–7.2 are only the tip of the iceberg; §7.3 uses different activations, different architectures and different mathematical tools to weave "first-order methods are not blind luck" into a denser net, but the edge of that net still stops at convergence and training loss.

41dfe1f6c3cc.zh: 為什麼需要這站？前面每節都很容易變成孤島：動量、Adam、SAM、Prop 5 各講各的。沒有一張全章地圖，你會以為「用了 Adam 或 SAM 就等於懂深度學習」。這一站就是把孤島用同一條訓練動線串起來，並在出口立牌：泛化，下一章以後還要再問。
41dfe1f6c3cc.en: Why do we need this stop? Each earlier section can easily become an island: momentum, Adam, SAM and Prop 5 each telling their own story. Without a map of the whole chapter, you would think "using Adam or SAM means understanding deep learning". This stop connects the islands along a single training route and puts up a sign at the exit: generalization still has to be asked about from the next chapter on.

1658daae8457.zh: 符號逐個拆：五段工具鏈，外加 §7.3 的延伸
1658daae8457.en: The symbols, one by one: the five-stage toolchain, plus the extensions in §7.3

4349888a0be3.zh: 本章優化主軸可以唸成五段，每段都有自己的符號，但骨架都是「算梯度、走一步」：
4349888a0be3.en: The chapter's optimization thread can be recited as five stages, each with its own symbols, but the skeleton is always "compute the gradient, take a step":

b5c1bd7b1352.zh: 基礎：梯度下降（學習率 $\eta$、線搜索、最陡下降）加上動量（KP-2 到 KP-5）；反向傳播（KP-6）用鏈式法則讓多層梯度算得起。
b5c1bd7b1352.en: Foundations: gradient descent (learning rate $\eta$, line search, steepest descent) plus momentum (KP-2 to KP-5); backpropagation (KP-6) uses the chain rule to make multilayer gradients affordable.

092ee676d35c.zh: 規模化：SGD 用單樣本近似全梯度（KP-7），mini-batch 與 epoch 在噪聲與穩定之間折衷（KP-8）；收斂率上，全梯度 $O(1/t)$，SGD 固定步長會在 $O(\eta)$ 鄰域晃（KP-9）。
092ee676d35c.en: Scaling up: SGD approximates the full gradient with a single sample (KP-7), and mini-batches and epochs trade off between noise and stability (KP-8); as for convergence rates, the full gradient gives $O(1/t)$, while SGD with a fixed step size wobbles in an $O(\eta)$ neighborhood (KP-9).

c34197adfff1.zh: 自適應步長：AdaGrad 累積梯度平方（KP-10）；RMSProp 改指數平均避免步長枯死；Adam 把動量（一階矩 $\boldsymbol{m}$）與 RMSProp（二階矩）加上偏差修正（KP-11）。
c34197adfff1.en: Adaptive step sizes: AdaGrad accumulates squared gradients (KP-10); RMSProp switches to an exponential average to keep the step size from dying out; Adam combines momentum (first moment $\boldsymbol{m}$) and RMSProp (second moment) with bias correction (KP-11).

6c9c198ae8ae.zh: 泛化導向優化：平坦極小值可能比較能遷移（KP-12）→ Vanilla SAM 的 min-max（KP-13）→ ESAM 的 SWP/SDS 與 ASAM 的尺度不變（KP-14）。
6c9c198ae8ae.en: Generalization-oriented optimization: flat minima may transfer better (KP-12) → Vanilla SAM's min-max (KP-13) → ESAM's SWP/SDS and ASAM's scale invariance (KP-14).

044e83b6df99.zh: 理論收尾：過參數化下 Prop 4/5 保證訓練損失可任意小、假坑消失、鞍點可逃（KP-15）。
044e83b6df99.en: Theoretical closing: under overparameterization, Prop 4/5 guarantee that the training loss can be made arbitrarily small, false pits vanish, and saddle points can be escaped (KP-15).

e1186756a44a.zh: §7.3 把同一句話寫到更多設定，不必背文獻編號，記住「三個方向」就夠：
e1186756a44a.en: §7.3 writes the same sentence for more settings; you don't need to memorize the reference numbers, just remember the "three directions":

29f6dfed7dd0.zh: 激活：二次、ReLU、Leaky ReLU 都有收斂或曲面分析，不是只有某一種 $\sigma$ 能被研究。
29f6dfed7dd0.en: Activations: quadratic, ReLU and Leaky ReLU all have convergence or loss-surface analyses; it is not just one particular $\sigma$ that can be studied.

f2254425409e.zh: 架構：收斂理論已長到 ResNet 這類殘差網，以及非 i.i.d. 的結構化資料。
f2254425409e.en: Architectures: convergence theory has grown to cover residual networks like ResNet, as well as non-i.i.d. structured data.

c4cb4480ca30.zh: 工具：臨界點長什麼樣、二元分類的損失曲面、深線性網的代數結構、寬網 GD 的誤差界——愈來愈不像「非凸所以放棄證明」。
c4cb4480ca30.en: Tools: what critical points look like, the loss surface of binary classification, the algebraic structure of deep linear networks, error bounds for GD on wide networks — less and less like "it's non-convex, so give up on proofs".

a137aab8e97b.zh: 數值真的算一遍：同一模型的兩張成績單
a137aab8e97b.en: Actually crunching the numbers: two report cards for the same model

643f374cc688.zh: 假設過參數化網（符合 Prop 5 那種「夠寬、資料有間隔」的精神）訓完之後，你拿到兩組數字：
643f374cc688.en: Suppose that after training an overparameterized network (in the spirit of Prop 5: "wide enough, data with a separation"), you get two sets of numbers:

4f2ff8d32ecf.en: Does this chapter's theory cover it?

4f6d078846fb.zh: 管：Prop 4/5、GD/SGD/Adam 都在把這欄往下壓
4f6d078846fb.en: Yes: Prop 4/5 and GD/SGD/Adam are all pushing this column down

c76597891dca.zh: 管：零損失的親戚，仍是訓練集
c76597891dca.en: Yes: a relative of zero loss, still on the training set

3b87f814e78c.en: No: the propositions do not guarantee it

1217364a7aab.zh: 不管：這就是泛化，尚未被本章收成定理
1217364a7aab.en: No: this is generalization, not yet turned into a theorem by this chapter

588a1cf084b8.zh: 再對一下「同一骨架上的兩個改良」各改了什麼。設某維度的梯度長期是 $g_t=0.2$，Adam 的二階矩估計大約 $v\approx(0.2)^{2}=0.04$，有效步長是 $\eta/\sqrt{v+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{Adam}}}$ 這一類（細節在 KP-11）；它改的是步長尺。SAM 若 $\rho=0.1$、$\nabla\mathcal{L}=(3,4)$，則 $\boldsymbol{\epsilon}^{*}=(0.06,0.08)$（KP-13），它改的是評估點：先走到最慘鄰居再量斜率。兩個數字都算得出來，職責完全不同——把訓練損失從 $0.50$ 壓到 $0.0008$ 的是優化成功；測試還留 $8\%$ 錯誤，說明健身房換了器材，故事沒結束。
588a1cf084b8.en: Now let's check what each of the "two improvements on the same skeleton" changes. Suppose the gradient in some dimension stays at $g_t=0.2$ for a long time; Adam's second-moment estimate is then about $v\approx(0.2)^{2}=0.04$, and the effective step size is of the form $\eta/\sqrt{v+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{Adam}}}$ (details in KP-11); what it changes is the ruler for the step size. For SAM with $\rho=0.1$ and $\nabla\mathcal{L}=(3,4)$, $\boldsymbol{\epsilon}^{*}=(0.06,0.08)$ (KP-13); what it changes is the evaluation point: first walk to the worst neighbor, then measure the slope. Both numbers can be computed, and their jobs are completely different — pushing the training loss from $0.50$ down to $0.0008$ is optimization succeeding; still having $8\%$ test error means the gym switched equipment, and the story is not over.

688a9d2bfa17.zh: 讀到這裡最舒服的結局會是：「理論證明了大模型為什麼泛化好。」反轉必須講白：沒有。 你確實可以在多項式時間內把訓練損失挖到 $\lt \epsilon$，ResNet 與 ReLU 也有愈來愈多收斂保證，這解釋的是「非凸但可優化」為什麼不是碰運氣。原文 §8 的第三句話才是章末真正的句號——優化通常成功，為何還能泛化，仍須追問。把「訓得動」與「測得好」畫等號，是整章最貴的誤會。
688a9d2bfa17.en: The most comfortable ending at this point would be: "The theory proved why large models generalize well." The twist has to be said plainly: it didn't. You really can dig the training loss down to $\lt \epsilon$ in polynomial time, and ReLU and ResNet have more and more convergence guarantees; what this explains is why "non-convex yet optimizable" is not a matter of luck. The third sentence of §8 in the original text is the chapter's real full stop — optimization usually succeeds, why it still generalizes must keep being asked. Equating "trainable" with "tests well" is the most expensive misunderstanding in the whole chapter.

0dc05c8c2feb.zh: 換成升學比喻：模擬考（訓練集）可以靠題庫刷到滿分，命題課綱保證「題目結構你練得完」（過參數化收斂）；學測（測試集）換了敘述、換了情境，滿分模擬考不自動變成學測保證班。Adam 像調整讀書節奏，SAM 像刻意找最容易錯的鄰近題型先做。現在自己對表：若有人說「我用了 Adam＋SAM，測試一定好」，他混掉了工具鏈的哪兩段？請用「步長 / 平坦谷 / 訓練損失 / 泛化」四個詞各寫一句，不看稿。
0dc05c8c2feb.en: Switch to an exam-prep metaphor: you can grind a question bank until you score full marks on the mock exams (the training set), and the syllabus guarantees "you can practice through every question structure" (overparameterized convergence); the real university entrance exam (the test set) changes the wording and the scenarios, and a perfect mock score does not automatically become a guarantee for the real exam. Adam is like adjusting your study pace; SAM is like deliberately doing the nearby question types you are most likely to get wrong first. Now check yourself: if someone says "I used Adam + SAM, so my test results will definitely be good", which two stages of the toolchain have they mixed up? Write one sentence each using the four terms "step size / flat valley / training loss / generalization", without looking at your notes.

fc3cb05b2bac.zh: 誤解「§7 已經解釋大模型泛化」。射程是訓練損失與可優化性；泛化是開放問題。
fc3cb05b2bac.en: Misconception: "§7 already explains generalization in large models". Its reach is training loss and optimizability; generalization is an open problem.

adb5ea2bfb30.zh: 誤解「Adam 結合的是線搜索與 SAM」。Adam 結合的是動量（一階矩）與 RMSProp（二階矩的指數平均），再加偏差修正。
adb5ea2bfb30.en: Misconception: "Adam combines line search and SAM". Adam combines momentum (first moment) and RMSProp (exponential average of the second moment), plus bias correction.

e4b45a241dca.zh: 誤解「只有全連接淺網能被分析」。§7.3 點名 ResNet、結構化資料、多種激活，理論正在往實務架構長。
e4b45a241dca.en: Misconception: "only shallow fully connected networks can be analyzed". §7.3 names ResNet, structured data and several activations; the theory is growing toward practical architectures.

d5b0e8b02ea7.zh: 誤解「能訓成功所以過擬合理論錯了、可以不用管正則」。訓練成功只說明坑挖得到；測起來好不好，仍可能要靠平坦解、資料、架構，本章沒發這張執照。
d5b0e8b02ea7.en: Misconception: "training succeeds, so overfitting theory is wrong and regularization can be ignored". Training success only says the pits can be dug; whether it tests well may still depend on flat solutions, the data and the architecture — this chapter has not issued that license.

e7775fd37fc5.zh: KP-2 到 KP-6：下山的腳法與反傳這座橋——沒有它們，後面的 Adam 與 SAM 都沒有梯度可改。
e7775fd37fc5.en: KP-2 to KP-6: the footwork for walking downhill and the bridge that is backprop — without them, the later Adam and SAM would have no gradient to modify.

befeb1c17ecf.zh: KP-7 到 KP-9：用噪聲換成本，以及你最多只能期望收到什麼速率。
befeb1c17ecf.en: KP-7 to KP-9: trading noise for cost, and the best rate you can hope to converge at.

cc29962bd413.zh: KP-10、KP-11：自適應尺；Adam 是預設選項之一，不是終點。
cc29962bd413.en: KP-10, KP-11: the adaptive ruler; Adam is one of the default choices, not the end point.

515aa62a821b.zh: KP-12 到 KP-14：從「喜歡平坦」到 min-max，再到遮罩、銳樣本、尺度尺。
515aa62a821b.en: KP-12 to KP-14: from "liking flatness" to min-max, then on to masks, sharp samples and the scale ruler.

a780000fe411.zh: KP-15：礦坑幾乎一樣深——為「訓得動」背書，刻意不為「測得好」背書。
a780000fe411.en: KP-15: the pits are almost equally deep — vouching for "trainable", deliberately not vouching for "tests well".

82ab242c107a.zh: 全章一句話重講：訓練神經網路就是在高維非凸曲面上做（隨機）梯度下降，反傳讓梯度算得起，Adam 調步長、SAM 偏平坦解，過參數化理論保證訓練損失通常能被壓下去；這整條鏈解釋的是「能訓成功」，不是「已懂泛化」。
82ab242c107a.en: The whole chapter restated in one sentence: training a neural network is doing (stochastic) gradient descent on a high-dimensional non-convex surface; backprop makes the gradients affordable, Adam tunes the step size, SAM favors flat solutions, and overparameterization theory guarantees the training loss can usually be pushed down; this entire chain explains "training succeeds", not "generalization is understood".

1a21ea8f6714.zh: 「反傳讓梯度算得起，Adam 調步、SAM 找平谷；這台練到沒阻力，換館還能不能舉，才是下一題。」
1a21ea8f6714.en: "Backprop makes gradients affordable, Adam tunes the step, SAM finds flat valleys; this machine feels effortless now, but whether you can still lift at a different gym is the next question."
